# 周易集解

**ID:** KR1a0008
**Custom ID:** ZB1a0007

**Source:** 四庫全書 文淵閣版, V7.7, p603
**Extent:** 17 卷

## Authors / Editors
- 李鼎祚 (唐朝) 撰

**Editions:** WYG

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The single most important Táng-period anthology of pre-Táng *Yì* commentary, compiled by [李鼎祚](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E9%BC%8E%E7%A5%9A) Lǐ Dǐngzuò of Zī zhōu (modern Zī zhōng 資中, Sìchuān) sometime after 755 CE while serving as *Zhùzuòláng* 著作郎 ("Director of Compositions") in the Imperial Library (*Bìshū shěng* 祕書省). The work systematically gathers commentary from thirty-five named pre-Táng masters and from the *Jiǔjiā Yì* 九家易 ("Nine-Houses *Yì*") and *Qián záodù* 乾鑿度 — preserving substantial fragments of the otherwise-lost Hàn *xiàngshù* 象數 commentaries ([孟喜](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%9F%E5%96%9C) Mèng Xǐ, [焦贛](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%84%A6%E8%B4%9B) Jiāo Gàn, [京房](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BA%AC%E6%88%BF) Jīng Fáng, [馬融](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A6%AC%E8%9E%8D) Mǎ Róng, [荀爽](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8D%80%E7%88%BD) Xún Shuǎng, [鄭玄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%84%AD%E7%8E%84) Zhèng Xuán, [宋衷](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%8B%E8%A1%B7) Sòng Zhōng, [虞翻](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%99%9E%E7%BF%BB) Yú Fān, [陸績](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E7%B8%BE) Lù Jì, [干寶](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%B9%B2%E5%AF%B6) Gān Bǎo, [王肅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E8%82%85) Wáng Sù, [姚信](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A7%9A%E4%BF%A1) Yáo Xìn, [王廙](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%BB%99) Wáng Yì, [張璠](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E7%92%A0) Zhāng Pán, [向秀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%90%91%E7%A7%80) Xiàng Xiù, [侯果](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BE%AF%E6%9E%9C) Hóu Guǒ, [蜀才](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%9C%80%E6%89%8D) Shǔcái, [翟元](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%BF%9F%E5%85%83) Dí Yuán, [崔憬](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%B4%94%E6%86%AC) Cuī Jǐng, etc.). Lǐ programmatically describes his project in the preface as *kān Fǔsì zhī yěwén, bǔ Kāngchéng zhī yìxiàng* 刋輔嗣之野文，補康成之逸象 — "to prune [王弼](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%BC%BC) Wáng Bì's wild words and supply what is missing from [鄭玄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%84%AD%E7%8E%84) Zhèng Xuán's images" — i.e. a corrective restoration of *xiàngshù* against the *yìlǐ* 義理 monopoly that had been imposed by [孔穎達](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%94%E7%A9%8E%E9%81%94) Kǒng Yǐngdá's *zhèngyì* a century earlier ([KR1a0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0007)).

Without this book, the entire Hàn *Yì* tradition would be unrecoverable: virtually every Qīng *kǎozhèng* recompilation of a Hàn *Yì* school ([王應麟](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E6%87%89%E9%BA%9F) Wáng Yīnglín on Zhèng [KR1a0003](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0003), [惠棟](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%83%A0%E6%A3%9F) Huì Dòng's augmented Zhèng [KR1a0004](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0004), [姚士粦](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A7%9A%E5%A3%AB%E7%B2%A6) Yáo Shìlín on Lù Jì [KR1a0005](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0005), [張惠言](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E6%83%A0%E8%A8%80) Zhāng Huìyán on Yú Fān, [馬國翰](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A6%AC%E5%9C%8B%E7%BF%B0) Mǎ Guóhàn on virtually all of them) draws principally on quotations preserved here. The Sìkù *tiyao* judges it "truly a precious antique manuscript" (*zhēn kě bǎo zhī gǔ jí* 真可寶之古笈).

The textual history is complex: Lǐ's own preface gives the work as eighteen *juàn* (ten of *jíjiě* + one appended *Lüèlì* of Wáng Bì + six of a separate work *Suǒyǐn* 索隱 + the preface = the original "eighteen-*juàn*" claim, which the Sìkù editors decode as 10 + 1 + 6 with the preface counted separately). The Hàn-Táng bibliographies record seventeen *juàn*; [晁公武](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%81%E5%85%AC%E6%AD%A6) Cháo Gōngwǔ and [李燾](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E7%87%BE) Lǐ Tāo of the Sòng saw a ten-*juàn* recension; [朱睦㮮](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E7%9D%A6%E3%AE%AE) Zhū Mùwēng's 1557 preface (嘉靖丁巳) likewise gives ten. [毛晉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AF%9B%E6%99%89) Máo Jìn's *Jígǔgé* 汲古閣 print of the late Míng arbitrarily redivided the surviving ten *juàn* into seventeen to make the count match the Tángshū entry, and thereby produced the present recension. The lost *Suǒyǐn* was a separate auxiliary work covering passages where the canonical text and commentaries were difficult to reconcile ("*kǎ ér páng yǐn* 錯綜旁引"); it was already lost by the early Sòng.

Lǐ's compilation reorders the canonical text in a peculiar way: he prefixes each of the sixty-four hexagrams with the relevant fragment of the *Xùguà zhuàn* 序卦傳 (the Wing explaining the order), modelled on the *Máoshī* 毛詩 practice of prefixing each ode with its *xiǎo xù* 小序 — an editorial choice that became standard in the *xiàngshù* tradition.

Composition window 755–800: notBefore is the conventional terminus post quem (the *Jiù Tángshū jīngjí zhì* records up to Kāiyuán prosperity and does not contain this work, hence Lǐ is post-An-Lushan); notAfter the conventional terminus ante quem of the late-eighth-century *Yì* school's reception of the work.

**Abstract**

[李鼎祚](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E9%BC%8E%E7%A5%9A) Lǐ Dǐngzuò is one of the most consequential mid-Táng *Yì* scholars and one of the most poorly documented: no entry in either the *Jiù Tángshū* or the *Xīn Tángshū liè zhuàn*, no surviving funerary inscription, no Tang-poetry corpus mentioning him. He signs his own preface as *Bìshū shěng zhùzuòláng* — a junior compositional post in the Imperial Library — and the only other secure datum is [袁桷](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A2%81%E6%A1%B7) Yuán Jué's Yuán-period record of a "Dǐngzuò Reading Terrace" at Zī zhōu (modern Sìchuān). The internal evidence places him post-755 (the An Lushan rebellion): his work is absent from the *Jiù Tángshū* bibliographic monograph (which records up to the high-Kāiyuán). The conventional reckoning places his active life in the second half of the eighth century. His own preface presents the work as a programmatic restoration of the *xiàngshù* tradition against the *yìlǐ* monopoly imposed by the *zhèngyì* commission a century earlier ([KR1a0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0007)).

The work's structure: under the [王弼](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%BC%BC) Wáng Bì arrangement of the base text, with each hexagram's own *Xùguà zhuàn* fragment prefixed (after the *Máoshī xiǎo xù* model), Lǐ assembles passage-by-passage commentary from his thirty-five masters. The signal preserved-fragments are of [虞翻](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%99%9E%E7%BF%BB) Yú Fān (the most extensively cited; [張惠言](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%B5%E6%83%A0%E8%A8%80) Zhāng Huìyán's later *Yú shì Yì* 虞氏易 is principally a redaction of these), of [荀爽](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8D%80%E7%88%BD) Xún Shuǎng (the *jíjiě* preserves perhaps two-thirds of the surviving Xún material), of [鄭玄](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%84%AD%E7%8E%84) Zhèng Xuán (the largest single block of surviving Zhèng *Yì* fragments), of [陸績](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E7%B8%BE) Lù Jì, [侯果](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BE%AF%E6%9E%9C) Hóu Guǒ, [崔憬](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%B4%94%E6%86%AC) Cuī Jǐng, and the *Jiǔjiā Yì* 九家易. The "Nine-Houses *Yì*" itself is a Hàn or post-Hàn composite drawing on nine masters of the Hàn line — its identity is not stable across the bibliographic record, and what reaches us is what Lǐ Dǐngzuò chose to call by that name.

The *Suǒyǐn* 索隱 ("Searching the Hidden"), Lǐ's separate auxiliary work, is recorded by him in the preface as a six-*juàn* companion treating "the [conjoined] warp-and-weft of root-and-shoot, phonetics and meanings"; it was already scattered and lost by the early Sòng and is known only from the Sìkù editors' decoding of his preface. (Several Qīng evidential scholars searched for it without success; the *Suǒyǐn* is the canonical exemplar of a "completely lost auxiliary by an extant author" in the *Yì* corpus.)

The textual history then runs through [晁公武](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%81%E5%85%AC%E6%AD%A6) Cháo Gōngwǔ's ten-*juàn* witness, [朱睦㮮](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E7%9D%A6%E3%AE%AE) Zhū Mùwēng's 1557 print (also ten *juàn*), [毛晉](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%AF%9B%E6%99%89) Máo Jìn's *Jígǔgé* late-Míng repagination as seventeen *juàn*, and the Sìkù WYG re-edition. The 1557 Zhū Mùwēng preface — preserved at the head of the WYG _000.txt and reproduced as a small monument of mid-Míng *Yì*-bibliographic argument — is itself a major source for the Sòng-Yuán reception of the work and its identification of pre-Táng *Yì* schools.

The Qīng evidential reception of the *Jíjiě* is enormous. Sūn Tángshū's 孫堂書 *Hàn Wèi èrshíyī jiā Yì zhù* 漢魏二十一家易註 (Qīng) is essentially a redaction of *Jíjiě* citations under master-by-master heads. Zhāng Huìyán's *Yú shì Yì* (1808 preface) is a redaction of the Yú Fān citations. [馬國翰](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%A6%AC%E5%9C%8B%E7%BF%B0) Mǎ Guóhàn's *Yùhán shānfáng jíyì shū* draws on *Jíjiě* citations across the canon. The standard modern critical edition is Lǐ Dàoxiáng 李道湘 / Wáng Fēnghǎi 王豐海 et al. at Zhōnghuá shūjú or the Bei-dà punctuated text in the *Shísān jīng zhùshū* corollary set; the Cài Jié 蔡傑 et al. modern collation is also widely cited.
